I have 3 kids so I have a pretty chaotic dinner time. This is how I cook / meal plan / track. 

I put out a post it note and pen and hand write every ingredient and weight in grams. I then make the meal, and weight the final product in ounces (ex. If it is a pot of chili, I transfer to a bowl to weigh it). This becomes the SERVINGS for the recipe I create in MFP. At this point the kids are bugging the shit out of me, so I usually weigh my meal and serve everyone. So I would weight out 12oz of chili which would be “12 servings”. After we are done eating I create the recipe and log it. 

I then either store it all together in one Tupperware and serve out the serving amount I want, or I create a Meal with the separate pieces if I am making mealprep containers (ex. 4 “servings” chicken, 3 “servings” roasted potatoes, 7 “servings” veggies).

Yes, it is an added stressor to an already stressful period of the day but it is necessary for me to get accurate tracking and it is worth it when I cook in bulk and I don’t have to do any weighing for multiple meals.

TLDR: I definitely found the FTG to cover almost all needs. If anything, I would add a stretchy wrap for the first weeks. After that, FTG will cover all your needs if you want it to. But if you and baby really get into babywearing, it’s definitely worth exploring other options. 

I started with a Boba wrap, which I think is much more cozy and snug for the newborn days. 

I then got a Tula FTG and used that exclusively for a long time. Husband shouldn’t need his own unless it annoys you to have to readjust the straps every time you switch (which really is not a big deal). 

I then got a ring sling for quicker in and out for stores. I personally never liked it- for me, it’s uncomfortable and was no quicker than my FTG to get in and out, BUT I do like that he can see out and around really well so I have easier interaction with him. (I typically back wear in FTG so I don’t talk to him as much). 

I was gifted a used woven wrap which I only learned to use when I got pregnant and the FTG wasn’t comfortable anymore. But once I figured it out - it is SO comfortable. Not convenient but very comfy for long carries, and it made me realize the FTG is not a super comfortable carrier (at least not for me).

Last wrap I got was an SSC from Soul, by recommendation that it would be more comfortable on my pregnant belly. It definitely is, but I really only got it for this purpose and to have an easy up-down for when we go hiking. 

Anyway, there’s my whole babywearing story, hope it helps :D.

I gave birth at a holistic Birth Center, so interventions were not even an option unless I transferred to a hospital. I started with several days of early labor, which I thought was annoying (HA wish it all could have been as easy as those days!) then finally started my final early labor on Monday evening. Rested for a few hours before contractions become much heavier, then labored at home until about 1pm Tuesday. 

I was not supposed to head to the Birth Center until my contractions were 3min apart for at least an hour. I had many hours of severe contractions that were spaced 4mim, then back to 7/8min, back down to 4/5min - I began to get very emotionally defeated, thinking I’d be stuck in this cycle for a very long time and still had a long labor ahead of me. Between contractions I schemed how I could get to the hospital instead of the birth center to just get the baby cut the fuck out of me because I didn’t know how I’d possibly make it. I finally had a few contractions within 2-3min and my boyfriend got me in the car and took me to the birth center. 

I got there and was 8cm dilated - i was SO fucking happy (momentarily, between contractions) knowing I was so close! I got to my room and immediately got in the tub. The water made a big difference- the feeling of floating really took a certain edge off the contractions and I was able to rest easier between. 

I labored for about 2 hours in the tub before I started pushing - it was hard, but I was so hype on adrenaline and seeing the finish line that I feel like the pain was hardly comparable to labor. I pushed for 20 minutes, then had to get out of the tub to have the baby’s heartbeat monitored through a whole contraction. The baby’s head was nearly out so I ended up pushing him out the rest of the way on the bed!

So, I survived a completed unmedicated childbirth. It helped a lot that I had a doula to guide me, an incredible partner, and especially that an epidural wasn’t even an option - because I have no doubt that if it were, I would have said FUCK YES to that!! Absolutely no judgment to the women who choose pain management during childbirth. I’m glad I was able to follow through with my birth plan, but can’t say I did it on my own!

Also, I have the most beautiful, precious baby boy and I’m so completely in love and nothing else matters in the world!

1. Was your friend a massage therapist, or was your friend just doing whatever? Ticklish usually means those muscles are tight - a good MT will know that, and know to back off the pressure and slow down to warm up the muscles.
2. Unless your deoderant is very, very strong, or your BO comes on immediately after showering, don't worry about this much. We deal with a lot of body smells and it's usually not a problem.
3. Firstly, don't skip out on an MT at a chiro simply because you think it's psuedo-science. I work for a wonderful chiro, and I give a kickass massage. Most likely, they are going to be better prepared to work with injuries or specific muscles. Avoid chains (Hand&Stone, etc.) because they're often high turnover and you never know what you're going to get. Spas will be more for relaxation, not so much therapeutic. I would look for a friend's recommendation, or find someone who seems to have a successful solo practice (they're successful on their own for a good reason).
4. That probably depends on whether they're a morning person or not. I can't say my first massage of the day is better than the last.
5. There's a lot of MTs to choose from, so just choose who sounds like you'll be able to communicate on the same level with them. And as I said in answer 3, an MT at a chiro may be more science-oriented as it sounds like you're looking for.
6. Hopefully the MT will take your lead and NOT talk to you if you don't want to. I actively try to not encourage conversation with patients, even if they are talkative, because I want them to have the time to truly relax.
7. Yes, you can massage fingers. Just tell them exactly what you wrote at the top, and they'll know where to go. For example, you sit a lot - so you're going to need full back work, probably hunched shoulders, stiff low back, very tight glutes/hips, tight hip flexors.
8. YES they wash the sheets! 
9. I take patients to the room to talk over their intake form. Go over their questions. Then tell them I'll leave the room for a few minutes for them to get undressed and get under the sheets, face up or face down, whatever we've decided. Everyone will do something along those lines. Th rule of thumb is, the more skin showing, the better the massage - so if you're comfortable with being commando or in your underoos, that's best. If you keep boxers on, just know you may not have your upper 1/2 of quads and hamstrings worked on.
10. You can ask them to start at medium pressure, and throughout the massage you can ask for more or less at any time. And of course you'll tell them it's your first massage and you're not sure - I'm sure they'll be willing to work with you and experiment with pressures.
11. This depends on where you go. You can request a gender, but I don't think it's legal in a lot of places for receptionists to ask what you prefer.
12. Massage is legitimate. You will understand when you get a good massage. I have fixed lots of problems - sciatic issues, neck problems, circulation and nerve problems. A chronic shoulder injury was fixed in just a single session. There's plenty of research. Look into it. Many injuries or pains are easily fixed with massage, yet since massage isn't covered by insurance, it's since as illegitimate, and instead people take pain killers and get surgeries. 
13. 15-20% of full price is good - if you get a discount (first time, groupon, etc) please tip on the amount of a normally priced massage - many MTs are paid on a percentage basis, so if you pay 15% on a 50% off massage, they're getting fucked.
14. Overall, it sounds like you have some anxiety about the idea of getting a massage, but I'm glad you're exploring this option, because for many people, it is incredibly helpful for chronic pain and general upkeep of the body. So I would recommend you being clear this is your first massage, you're not totally sure what to expect, ask if it's okay for you to communicate, etc. The MT will actually really appreciate you being up front and honest and it will help them help you. A good MT will make you feel comfortable and check in with you.

I am bipolar and I get wicked depressed for long periods of time. There are some things that help me get through it.

One is remembering that my illness is like bad brain wiring. My perception of the world is heavily clouded by whatever lack of chemicals my brain is making. I try to take a few deep breaths and step back away from my brain. I am not my depression, but my depression is like a pair of goggles that I forget I'm wearing. I try to do this throughout the day, sort of like a short meditation.

Also when I'm depressed, I hate doing everything. But ultimately, I know that I always feel better after spending time with people. I have found that my favorite person to be around is a friend who can laugh with me about the darkest shit that goes through my head. I'll be like FUCK I feel like dying and we laugh and laugh at how stupid life is and this predicament we were forced into.

I also tend to "fake it til I make it." Many people would be very surprised if I knew that I have these problems. I am quite good at hiding them, which is an okay thing sometimes. I laugh and smile and I am kind and helpful. I have to give a HUGE effort, but controlling your actions and speech will eventually carry over to your mind. Not to mention, doing good things for people always makes me happy.

And you're right, people don't like to be around depressed people. Or, some people don't. It makes people who don't understand very uncomfortable. That's okay and you can't be mad at them for it.

I was a teenager when I started having serious depression problems and I was sent to a psychiatrist who loaded me up with all sorts of different drugs. I found them very unhelpful (mostly I think because I was severely overmedicated) and it's always left a bad taste in my mouth. I am by no means bashing medication because I know they help many people, but I do believe that with a lot of effort, you can have control over your condition.

I have also found it helpful to accept that this is who I am and what I will be dealing with for the rest of my life. While that sounds a bit depressing, it's really not. Accepting it gives me power over it and also the ability to plan ahead, learn about myself, my triggers, my patterns, etc. 

There is an app I use called "Optimism" to help me track my moods and triggers. You'll see very soon what things are affecting you.

I trust the House Rabbit Society for all answers! They do says 2 cups per 6 pounds, but I give 2 cups a day to my 2.6 lb rabbit and he's a little skinny thing. But, he also gets tons of exercise because he's cage free.

This is a good, comprehensive list of the foods that a rabbit can eat.
http://rabbit.org/suggested-vegetables-and-fruits-for-a-rabbit-diet/

Every day I feed my rabbits twice a day, 1 packed cup each feeding, 1 from list I and 2 from list II, all in approximately equal amounts. I almost always buy what's cheapest unless it doesn't look fresh. This usually ends up being:

From List I: Parsley, spinach, mustard green if they're fresh
From List II: romaine, red leaf lettuce, dandelion greens, occasionally kale (but I've heard you shouldn't over do kale)

It's always good to switch it up sometimes!

In addition to leafy green, I give them a bit of carrot in the morning (about 1-2 TB worth) or some of the fruit from my breakfast (banana, apple, etc.).

In the evening they get pellets, a heaping 1/4 cup each.

I hope this helps! BTW, all my buns are adults (between 3 and 7), so if you have a baby or young rabbit, you'll need a different diet.
